briefs.r110_1:
Use this checklist for each submission as of 1 Mar 2026.

1. Length – ≥22 pages (22 counts).  
2. Format – either the official template **or** at least three years of revision history documented.  
3. Venue overlap – if presented at a Tier‑1 venue, the presentation must be >18 months before the deadline; exactly 18 months fails.  
4. Prior rounds – accepted manuscripts are ineligible unless ≥5 years have passed since that round (exactly 5 is OK).  
5. Paired submissions – only two manuscripts may be paired; each meets R1 and R2, and at least one satisfies R3.  
6. Track D – replaces R2 with exactly two endorsements; no other exemptions.  
7. Retraction – any open retraction makes the submission automatically RETURNED.  
8. Figures – total must lie between 8 and 45 inclusive (70 allowed for a pair).  
9. If figures are below the minimum, pad to 8 and label PADDED; exceeding the maximum returns immediately.  
10. Withdrawals reset the R3 clock to the withdrawal date.
briefs.r110_2:
Check each manuscript against the following checklist, stopping at the first failure unless a later rule overrides it.

1. Length ≥ 22 pages (exactly 22 counts).  
2. Either use the official template **or** provide ≥3 years of revision history.  
3. If presented at a Tier‑1 venue, the presentation must be >18 months before 1 Mar 2026; exactly 18 months fails.  
4. Prior Meridian acceptance is disallowed unless ≥5 years have passed.  
5. Paired submissions: exactly two manuscripts; each meets rules 1–2, and at least one satisfies rule 3.  
6. Track D bypasses rule 2 but requires exactly two endorsements.  
7. Any open retraction forces RETURNED (overrides all).  
8. Figures 8‑45 inclusive (paired up to 70).  
9. If figures are below the minimum, PAD the manuscript; excess figures cause RETURNED.  
10. A withdrawal resets venue clock for rule 3.

Result: HANDLED if no rule fails, otherwise RETURNED or PADDED as specified.
briefs.r110_3:
Read each submission in the order below, stopping at the first rule that disqualifies it.

1. Check R7; any open retraction → RETURNED immediately.  
2. Verify length (R1). Fewer than 22 pages → RETURNED.  
3. Apply R6 if submitted to Track D: ignore R2 but require exactly two endorsements; otherwise enforce R2 (template or ≥3‑year revision history) → FAIL → RETURNED.  
4. Assess venue overlap (R3) unless a withdrawal resets the clock per R10.  
5. For prior‑round acceptances, apply R4.  
6. If it is a paired submission, ensure exactly two manuscripts satisfy R1 and R2; at least one meets R3.  
7. Count figures (R8). Below minimum → PADDED; above maximum → RETURNED.  

If none of the above returns, verdict is HANDLED.
briefs.r110_4: Check each manuscript against every rule in order; any failure (except the special padding case) yields RETURNED. R1: ≥22 pages (exactly 22 passes). R2: must use official template or have ≥3‑year revision log, unless Track D (R6) applies. R3: Tier‑1 presentations older than 18 months count; exactly 18 months fails. R4: prior acceptance within <5 years blocks handling; withdrawals reset the R3 clock (R10). R5: paired submissions allowed only as a set of two, each meeting R1 and R2, with at least one satisfying R3. R6: Track D skips R2 but requires exactly two endorsements. R7 overrides all – any open retraction is RETURNED. R8/9: figures 8‑45 (or up to 70 for pairs); if below minimum, PADDED; above maximum, RETURNED.
briefs.r110_5:
Read each submission sequentially through the rules, stopping at the first rule that forces a decision.

1. Check R7; any open retraction → RETURNED immediately.  
2. Verify length (R1) and figure count (R8). If figures are below eight, apply R9: pad to eight and label PADDED unless another rule later fails, in which case RETURNED.  
3. Apply R2 unless the paper is in Track D, where R6 replaces it with the requirement of exactly two endorsements.  
4. Evaluate venue timing (R3) and prior‑round age (R4); both must meet their “more than” or “at least” thresholds.  
5. For paired submissions enforce R5 and the higher figure maximum (70). The final verdict is HANDLED only if no rule rejects it.
briefs.r150_0: Follow these steps in order. First check length: the manuscript must have at least 22 pages; exactly 22 counts as sufficient. Next verify format: it either uses the official template or includes documented revision history covering three years or more. Then examine venue overlap: if the paper was presented at a Tier‑1 venue, the presentation date must be more than 18 months before the March 1 2026 deadline; exactly 18 months fails. Look at prior rounds: an acceptance in any earlier Meridian round blocks handling unless five full years have passed since that round; a withdrawal does not count as acceptance and resets the venue clock to the withdrawal date. For paired submissions, ensure there are exactly two manuscripts, each meeting length and format, and that at least one satisfies the venue rule. Track D papers skip the format requirement but must carry precisely two endorsements. Finally check figures: total must be 8‑45 (70 for pairs). If below minimum, pad to eight and mark PADDED; if above maximum, RETURNED.
briefs.r150_1: Use this checklist in order. 1️⃣ Length: manuscript must have ≥22 pages; exactly 22 counts. 2️⃣ Format: either the official template OR at least three years of documented revision history. 3️⃣ Venue overlap: if presented at a Tier‑1 venue, it is only acceptable when the presentation occurred more than 18 months before the March 1 2026 deadline (exactly 18 months does not qualify). 4️⃣ Prior rounds: an earlier Meridian acceptance blocks handling unless five full years have passed since that round (five years exactly is fine). 5️⃣ Paired submissions: allowed for exactly two papers; each must meet rules 1 and 2. At least one of the pair must satisfy rule 3, the other may not. 6️⃣ Track D: exempts rule 2 but requires exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient. 7️⃣ Retraction: any open retraction disqualifies the paper regardless of other rules. 8️⃣ Figures: count must be between 8 and 45 inclusive (70 allowed for a pair). 9️⃣ Figure adjustment: if below minimum, pad to eight and label PADDED; excess figures cause RETURNED. 🔟 Withdrawals reset the venue clock for rule 3.
briefs.r150_2:
Start with R1: the paper must be at least 22 pages; exactly 22 counts as OK. Then apply R2: either use the official template or provide three documented revision years. For Track D submissions skip R2 and instead require exactly two endorsements (R6); no other rule is waived.

Next check venue history (R3). A Tier‑1 presentation is acceptable only if it occurred more than 18 months before 1 March 2026; exactly 18 months fails. For any prior Meridian acceptance, apply R4: the previous round must be at least five years earlier; a withdrawal does not count as an acceptance and resets the R3 clock to the withdrawal date (R10).

If the paper is part of a paired submission, ensure there are exactly two manuscripts, each meeting R1 and R2, and that at least one meets R3. Figure limits follow R8; if below eight, pad to eight and label PADDED (R9). Any other violation yields RETURNED. If all applicable rules pass, mark HANDLED.
briefs.r150_3:
Follow this exact sequence for every submission.

1. If the manuscript carries an open retraction notice, immediately mark it **RETURNED** (R7 overrides everything).

2. Determine whether it is a paired submission. If so, verify there are exactly two manuscripts; each must meet R1 (≥22 pages) and R2 (template or ≥3‑year revision history). If either fails, the pair is **RETURNED**.

3. For each manuscript apply R6: if submitted to Track D, ignore R2 but require exactly two endorsements; otherwise enforce R2 normally.

4. Check venue overlap (R3). The presentation must be more than 18 months before 1 Mar 2026, unless a withdrawal occurred—in that case use the withdrawal date as the presentation date (R10).

5. Apply prior‑round rule (R4): an earlier acceptance is allowed only if at least five years have passed.

6. Count figures. If the count is below the minimum (8 for single, 8–70 for paired) pad to the minimum and record **PADDED** (R9). If it exceeds the maximum, **RETURNED**.

7. After all applicable rules are satisfied, label the manuscript **HANDLED**.
briefs.r150_4:
To decide the verdict for each submission, use this checklist as of 1 March 2026.

1. Retraction (R7). If an open retraction notice exists, mark RETURNED; no other rule applies.
2. Length (R1). Must have ≥ 22 pages (exactly 22 is ok).
3. Format (R2). Accept if the official template is used or revision history spans ≥ 3 years. Track‑D papers skip this (see R6).
4. Venue overlap (R3). Tier‑1 presentations must be > 18 months before the deadline; exactly 18 months fails.
5. Prior round acceptance (R4). Accepted previously only if ≥ 5 years have passed; withdrawals are not acceptances.
6. Paired submission (R5). Exactly two manuscripts may be linked; each meets R1 and R2, and at least one also satisfies R3.
7. Track D (R6). Require exactly two endorsements; R2 is waived but all other rules stay.
8. Figures (R8‑R9). Count 8–45 figures normally, up to 70 for pairs. Below minimum → PADDED; above maximum → RETURNED.

If none of the above trigger a return, issue HANDLED.
briefs.r150_5:
Use this checklist in order.

1. Length (R1): at least 22 pages; exactly 22 counts.

2. Format (R2): accept if the official template is used **or** there are ≥3 years of documented revisions.

3. Venue overlap (R3): a Tier‑1 presentation must be more than 18 months before 1 Mar 2026; exactly 18 months fails.

4. Prior rounds (R4): an earlier Meridian acceptance blocks handling unless ≥5 years have passed. Withdrawals do not count as acceptances and reset the R3 clock to the withdrawal date (R10).

5. Paired submissions (R5): allowed only for exactly two papers; each must satisfy R1 and R2, and at least one must meet R3.

6. Track D (R6): exempt from R2 but needs exactly 2 endorsements; no other exemptions.

7. Retraction (R7): any open retraction makes the paper RETURNED regardless of other rules.

8. Figures (R8‑R9): count must be 8–45 inclusive (70 for a pair). Below minimum, pad to 8 and mark PADDED; above maximum, RETURNED.

If all applicable rules pass, verdict is HANDLED.

H1_beta_below_half.note: interval decision, not a p-value: the claim is about a magnitude, and a p-value against a nil null answers a question nobody asked

H3_sender_less_responsive.decision_rule: paired sign-flip permutation, Holm-corrected, one-sided by design: beta_receiver > beta_sender

multiplicity.note: H1-H4 are one family (preregistration section 8). H1 and H2 are interval decisions with no p-value, so Holm divides alpha among the members that use one. The recorded_* quantities are not hypotheses and are not in the family.
